headline: Committee defers Aloha House care item and East Maui Water Authority budget review

meeting.body: Maui County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee
meeting.summary: The committee deferred both items without objection: Aloha House's substance abuse care, and the East Maui Water Authority's operations and fiscal year 2026 budget. The authority's director said a capacity update is due in the next couple of weeks.
meeting.recap: The committee met Monday, March 9, 2026.[[0:00:29]] The first item was Continuum of Care for Substance Abuse, focused on Aloha House.[[0:05:32]] The CEO of Maui Behavioral Health Resources said Aloha House has served the community since 1977.[[0:07:20]] She said Aloha House is about 85% funded by Medicaid.[[0:15:24]] She said federal Medicaid cuts in the "big beautiful bill" are starting to have impacts.[[0:15:32]] She said wildfire work in Lāhainā drew nurses and counselors away with higher pay.[[0:34:55]] She said the gap is mostly payroll, especially nursing staff.[[0:43:51]] She said about 50% of people who come to Aloha House are unhoused.[[0:50:03]] The committee deferred the item without objection.[[1:15:30]] The second item reviewed the East Maui Water Authority's operations and fiscal year 2026 budget.[[1:15:45]] The director said the authority has nine employees in eight positions, because two are half-time.[[1:20:46]] She said the authority awarded $75,000 to five grantees.[[1:28:10]] The grant coordinator said applicants asked for over $200,000 in total.[[1:38:07]] The director said an update on the authority's capacity to manage the system is coming in the next couple of weeks.[[1:52:53]] The committee deferred the item without objection.[[1:53:50]]
meeting.next: The authority is preparing a plan and an update that includes its capacity for managing the system.

moments.q: "I know my gap is about 500,000 right now. That's our gap."
East Maui Water Authority presentation begins
"We were able to award our $75,000 to five grantees."

issues.oneLine: The East Maui Water Authority presented a review of its operations and fiscal year 2026 budget.
issues.why: The grant coordinator said grant requests topped $200,000, so not all qualified applicants could be funded.
issues.next: The director said an update on the authority's capacity to manage the system will come out in the next couple of weeks.
issues.brief: The director said fiscal year 2026 is the authority's first year of full operation.[[#1]] The authority has nine employees in eight positions, because two are half-time.[[#2]] The authority awarded $75,000 to five grantees.[[#3]] The director said the mayor is leading ongoing talks with county departments and others about acquiring water infrastructure.[[#4]]
